---
title: Vector
description: "A fixed-width numeric vector supplied by another system."
---

Your application may already have a merchant representation from another
system. `Vector` lets the payment model use that supplied numeric evidence
alongside the amount and merchant name. The coordinates must have a fixed
width and be available at the payment's decision time.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    merchant_embedding=rf.Vector(n_dim=4),
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
merchant_embedding: [0.12, -0.03, 0.44, 0.08]
disputed: false
```

The four coordinates illustrate the supplied shape; set `n_dim` to the actual
width your application supplies. Use [Text](text.qmd) to
encode strings and [Branch](branch.qmd) for repeated transaction records.

## Input and options

Each valued input must be an Arrow list or fixed-size list with exactly
`n_dim` numeric, non-null elements. Values convert to `float32`. A null vector
is a separate field state; null elements inside a valued vector are invalid.
A vector with a NaN or infinite element is not a measurement: it takes the
`other` [value state](index.qmd#value-state) with zero content, for inputs and
targets, so one bad element cannot poison training.
relflow does not fit a vector normalizer: prepare coordinate scales upstream.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `n_dim` | required | Positive vector width. |
| `jitter` | `rf.Jitter()` | Training noise in supplied coordinate units. |
| `objective` | `"l2"` | Reconstruction loss: `"l1"` or `"l2"`. |

Jitter changes finite coordinates of valued training inputs before projection.
Targets remain pristine. Both settings of `jitter.normalize` use the same
coordinate space; see [Jitter](../reference/jitter.qmd).

## Learning and output

Reconstruction combines state cross entropy with content loss on valued
targets. MAE and RMSE metrics use the supplied coordinate scale.

In [prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd), null
ancestor records preserve their structural holes. `rf.Writer` rejects these
fixed-width vectors when PyArrow cannot round-trip them through Parquet; use
Arrow IPC for affected tables.

Prediction `content` is `fixed_size_list<float32>[n_dim]`. When the most likely
predicted state is non-valued, the writer emits a zero vector. Zeros therefore
do not establish whether a vector was observed; read the shared `state` and
`inferred` members in the [prediction envelope](../reference/prediction-output.qmd).

Use [shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options)
to make the vector a target or export a contextual embedding. That exported
embedding has the model width and is distinct from the supplied vector.
